name: Amplitude
oneLiner: The megaphone made literal and accountable: brand blue at the origin, Google's 5% floor as the innermost dashed ring, and three dated client outcomes pinned to the outer arcs, so the first screen is an input/output record on warm paper with one vermilion signal instead of a claim on a blue wall.
concept:
Nonprofit Megaphone's name promises amplification, and the current site says 'loud' the only way the category knows how: a saturated blue field. Amplitude replaces the blue with the physics of the metaphor, then makes the physics accountable. Every key surface is built from one diagram: an origin (the brand's own #0A23A2 dot, with a named account lead holding a $10,000/month grant beside it), rays leaving it up-and-right in the direction the existing mark already points, seven concentric arcs that gain weight as they travel, and level bars that rise at each arc's crossing of the output axis. The innermost ring is dashed and labelled 'Google's 5% CTR floor', so policy literacy is visible before the first scroll. Three real outcomes (COPD Foundation 300+ screenings/month, UNCF $38,000/month in donations, Solar Sister +3,000% search traffic) are pinned exactly where a ray meets an arc, each with vertical, twelve-month period and a case-file link, so a board-forwarding ED reads a record, not a promise. Real sound attenuates; on this site the signal grows, which is precisely NPM's claim, and every chip proves it with a date.

The diagram is declared in two layers. The geometry (rays, arcs, bars, trace, origin ring, ruled grid) is decorative and lives in one aria-hidden inline SVG sized to its grid column. Everything that carries information (the floor label, the lead chip, the three outcome chips, the axis label) is real DOM text, and a visually hidden figcaption states the whole argument in one sentence. That split is also what lets the hero degrade: when the hero container drops below 960px the arc field is swapped for the stacked level bar, the same component the phone hero uses, and the h1 scales with container units so it always holds two lines. Motion is pure CSS (arcs grow from the origin, bars rise, chips fade up, 1.4s total) and collapses to the final static state under prefers-reduced-motion; no JavaScript is required for any of it.

The panel's sharpest critiques were that trust was carried by geometry rather than evidence and that the field had no human in it. Both are fixed at the source: the account lead sits at the origin as a person, Amber Snow's portrait and 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy' sit under the primary CTA, and the trust ledger is a framed Letter from Google (Michelle Hurtado at 21px serif), a status ticker with an 'as of' date, and a typographic client roll set in five voices between hairlines like a donor wall. The register stays confident calm with a pulse: warm paper, near-black ink, one vermilion for arcs and the single emphasised headline word, a darker vermilion for buttons and small labels so every piece of text clears AA, and the mark's blue kept exactly where the brand lives: the logo tile, the origin dot, the Google stamp and the focus ring.
distinctFrom: It is the only direction whose signature is generated from the brand's own mark (the up-and-right vector rendered as rays, arcs and level bars on warm paper with a vermilion signal) rather than borrowed from a category like a newspaper, a civic form, a signed letter or the current blue wall.

palette.note: Warm unbleached ground for every page; replaces the #0000FF field. The 32px ruled hairline (5% ink) appears only behind the signal field and the outcomes ledger, never under body copy.

Outcome chips, case-file cards, reporting panels. 1px hairline border, 6px radius, a 10px paper halo so chips sit cleanly over arcs (6px on the ink lead chip so it never clips the origin ring), shadow 14px/32px at 14% ink.
Headlines, body, level bars, the lead chip and the guarantee band background. Never pure black; also the error-state colour so red never means alarm. Body copy uses #3A3C48 (9.6:1 on paper).
Mono labels, eyebrows, captions, periods and sources. 5.4:1 on paper, 6.1:1 on white. Client roll wordmarks use #4A4C58 (7.5:1).
Rules, borders, ledger lines, chart gridlines, the seam between copy and field. #ECE8DF for rules inside white chips.

The seven arcs (max 3px stroke, opacity capped at .6), the signal trace, the tallest level bar, the chip pins, the eyebrow dot, active nav underline, chart series one, and exactly one word per headline. 3.6:1 on paper, so large text (>= 24px bold) only; never a background, never a fill, never text under 24px.
Resting button colour: white text measures 5.1:1. Hover and pressed #B7311C (6.1:1). Only buttons use this as a fill.
Any vermilion text under 24px: the 5% floor label and dashed ring, the 'Read the guarantee' link. 5.3:1 on paper, so 11px mono labels pass AA.

Kept visibly present as the source of the signal: the logo tile, the origin dot of every diagram, the 'Letter from Google' stamp, the focus ring, Google Partner badge contexts, chart series two, links in long-form, and the contained 'One of nine' band. Never a full-bleed wall. Tint #FBE3DC is the halo around the origin and the selected-row fill.

typography.display: Bricolage Grotesque (Google Fonts, variable): 800 at opsz 96 for h1/h2 and ticker figures; 700 for chip and level-bar values. Never used below 24px; locked to two Webflow heading classes plus one 'figure' class.
typography.body: Hanken Grotesk (Google Fonts): 400 body, 500 nav and UI, 600 buttons, chip org names and inline emphasis, 700 for the wordmark (15px desktop, 14px phone) and the heavy voice in the client roll. All four families load from fonts.googleapis.com only; no Fontshare or self-hosted fonts.
typography.mono: Geist Mono (Google Fonts): 400/500 for eyebrows, labels, periods, sources, the 15 MIN / 2 MIN tags, the status ticker and the 'as of' line. Instrument Serif (400 + italic) is a confined fourth voice: only the Letter from Google quote (21px desktop, 19px phone) and the client roll (20px small caps and italic).
typography.scaleNotes: Desktop h1 60px / .96 / -0.04em (clamp(40px, 5cqi, 60px) so it always holds two lines in its 528px column), sentence case, exactly one word in signal vermilion, tabular figures off in headlines and on everywhere else. h2 52px / 1.0 / -0.03em. h3 28px / 1.15 / -0.02em. Body 17px / 1.55; hero sub 18px / 1.5 at max-width 480px; phone body and sub 16px / 1.5. Chip values 24px Bricolage 700 with a 12px Hanken 500 unit; chip org names 13px Hanken 600; chip labels, periods, sources and every mono label 11px, uppercase, 0.06-0.14em tracking (11px is the floor across the whole system; nothing is set smaller). Eyebrows and labels are the only uppercase text. Buttons 52px tall (40px in the nav, 36px in the phone nav), 15-16px Hanken 600, 5px radius, with an 11px mono time tag. Ticker figures 28px Bricolage 800 over 11px mono labels. Spacing is an 8px base: nav 76, hero 600, trust ledger ~150 on desktop (whole frame 829px); 96/128px section padding below the fold. Every figure carries unit and date ('$48M+ · as of Sep 2026') as a CMS rule.

layout:
- Grid: 12 columns, 1200px container, 48px gutters at desktop, 24px tablet, 16px phone; vertical rhythm on 8px. Sections are separated by a 1px ink rule and a numbered mono label (01, 02, 03) rather than cards; the origin/arc/bar token set appears at most three times per page (hero, services meter, eligibility checker). Every diagram ships as final-state static SVG or CSS first.
- 00 Nav (76px, hairline below): #0A23A2 mark tile + 'Nonprofit Megaphone' Hanken 700 with an 11px mono sub-line; Services, Our work, Happy clients, Team, Blog; 'Get a free quote →' mono link (existing landing page); 'Book a free call' CTA with the four-bar level glyph that rises like a VU meter on hover. Past the hero the nav gains a 1px ink rule and the CTA compresses to glyph + label.
- 01 Hero (600px, 600px copy column / 600px field): eyebrow 'One of nine inaugural Google-certified Ad Grant agencies'; h1 '$10,000 a month, carried further.' (further in vermilion); sub naming the $10,000/month grant and the 5% floor; action row = primary 'Book a free call · 15 MIN' + ink-outline 'Am I eligible? · 2 MIN' at equal 52px height; fine print on one line '100% grant-acquisition guarantee · Google Ad Grants Certified · 60+ team'; guarantee block with Amber Snow's portrait, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy', and a 'Read the guarantee' link. Field: blue origin dot on the seam, dashed labelled 5% floor ring (r 72), seven arcs at 60px pitch, three rays each passing through one chip pin, level bars at every arc/axis crossing, a signal trace off the right edge, 'Output · 12-month periods' axis label, the lead chip at the origin, three outcome chips pinned at r 252 / 312 / 372 with vertical, period and case-file link, reading order by distance. Below 960px container width the field swaps for the stacked level bar.
- 02 Trust ledger (ink rule above, hairline below): row one = framed 'Letter from Google' stamp, Michelle Hurtado's name and title in 11px mono, her quote in Instrument Serif 21px, beside a status ticker 780+ / $48M+ / 100% in 28px Bricolage 800 with 'Status ticker · as of Sep 2026'; row two = 'Among 780+ clients' followed by UNCF, Scouting America, COPD Foundation, YWCA Chicago, Earthwatch, Solar Sister, AAU, JFCS set in five typographic voices between hairlines.
- 03 The rules (policy literacy): three-column hairline table, Requirement / What Google does if you miss it / What we do about it, covering 5% CTR, conversion tracking, single-word keywords, account structure, monthly login, geo-targeting, quality score; dashed vermilion 5% marker in the CTR row; sourced footnote to Google's policy page with date.
- 04 Eligibility checker (rep-free exit): three questions (org type, country, working website) beside a mini signal diagram that completes one arc per answer; a 'yes' fills the outer arc in signal tint and offers the call; hospitals, schools and governments get an honest 'you're not eligible, here's why' card quoting Google's definition.
- 05 Outcomes ledger: hairline table with Organization, Vertical, Input, Outcome, Period, Source; twelve rows drawn from the case files, filterable by the 12 verticals; row hover fills with signal tint; each row carries 'Open case file' and 'Forward to board (PDF)'. 32px ruled grid behind the table only.
- 06 What it costs: flat monthly fee statement with the published range if leadership approves it, never a percentage of spend; the seven services as a hairline price list (Ad Grant management, Website SEO, Content creation, VisitorEmail, Google Remarketing, Microsoft Advertising, Spanish ad creation) under a services level meter (seven rising bars, Ad Grant tallest), the second appearance of the token set. Price is a screening question, so it sits before the team.
- 07 One of nine (contained #0A23A2 band, not full-bleed): the inaugural Google-certified agency fact, Google's 8x conversion-value stat for certified-managed grantees with its source, Google Partner badge with its clear-space rules, Inc. 5000 x4; arcs at low opacity in white behind.
- 08 Your team, named: six to eight black-and-white eye-level rectangular headshots with role and 'Nonprofits I support' captions; the cabin-retreat candid full-bleed with a thin vermilion rule beneath; copy stating who the prospect's named point of contact will be.
- 09 Reporting, shown: a real monthly report as a light console panel with named client and month, utilisation vs the $10,000 cap, CTR vs the dashed 5% floor, compliance ticks, mono REDACTED tags where needed; beside it the one-sentence month signed by a named account lead with photo and date.
- 10 Guarantee band (ink background): the $25 CEO guarantee in 52px Bricolage 800 with Amber Snow named and pictured, the 'person, not a policy' line, single CTA.
- 11 FAQ: five plain-language questions in a hairline accordion (why pay for something free; will it raise money, answered honestly; who is on my account; what if we get suspended; how long to acquire), each with a dated source line where a policy is cited.
- 12 Final CTA row: the hero action pair repeated verbatim plus 'See a real account report' ghost link opening a redacted PDF.
- 13 Footer: four columns, newsletter, address, socials, client-login link; 780+ used consistently; print stylesheet shipped for case files and the guarantee page.
imagery: No illustration system and no stock photography. Four image types only. First, the signal geometry: inline SVG arcs, rays, level bars and the origin dot generated from a small token set (origin, angle, ring pitch 60px, max stroke 3px, max opacity .6, dashed 5% floor ring at r 72), exported as final-state static SVG per breakpoint and sized to its grid column with viewBox and preserveAspectRatio xMinYMid slice; on phones and narrow containers the same data is rendered as the stacked level bar in plain CSS. Second, real photography of NPM's 60 people: black-and-white, eye-level, rectangular crops on warm paper for the team section; small colour rectangular crops of the named account lead and of Amber Snow in the hero (the mockups carry CSS placeholder frames with role='img' labels until the shoot). Third, real screens: the actual monthly report and the Google Ad Grants account view as light console panels with mono labels, named client and month, timestamps, and visible mono REDACTED tags instead of blur. Fourth, the client roll as typography: mixed Instrument Serif small caps, italic, tracked Hanken caps, Geist Mono and heavy Hanken, hairline-divided, so it reads as a donor wall and needs no logo licensing. Iconography is a single 1.5px ink stroke set built from arc, ray, bar and dot (the eligibility button carries a blue origin dot and two vermilion arcs). Data viz: paper ground, hairline gridlines, vermilion series one, brand blue series two, tabular figures, unit and period on every chart, a dashed vermilion horizontal line for Google's 5% CTR floor wherever CTR is charted, sourced footnote under every chart. Beneficiary photography appears only inside case files, with permission, never as homepage decoration.
motion: Static first, motion second, and nothing depends on JavaScript. 1. Hero load (pure CSS, shipped in the mockup): the origin pulses once in brand blue, the dashed floor and labels fade in, the seven arcs grow outward from the origin with an 80ms stagger (transform-origin at the origin, opacity to each arc's capped value), the level bars rise 60ms apart, the signal trace draws across the bar tops, the lead chip and the three outcome chips fade and translate 8px up in order of distance; 1.4s total, copy readable from frame one. 2. Phone: the three level bars extend from the origin edge with a 150ms stagger. 3. CTA: the four-bar glyph rises like a VU meter on hover with a 60ms stagger; pressed buttons darken from #C93A22 to #B7311C. 4. Below the fold (optional GSAP + ScrollTrigger sprint, native scroll only, no Lenis, JS budget under 300kB): sections reveal with 12px translate and opacity; the services meter and the checker draw on at 30% in view; ledger rows re-sort with FLIP; the ticker counts up with tabular figures and a static 'as of' date. 5. prefers-reduced-motion: every animation is wrapped in a no-preference media query, so reduced-motion users get the final state instantly with no keyframes at all. 6. Never: WebGL, kinetic type, parallax on photography, autoplaying video, scroll-jacking, red on error states.
mobile: The 390px hero is a different composition, not a shrunken arc field. Nav (60px): 32px mark tile + 'Nonprofit Megaphone' 14px, a 36px 'Book a call' button with the level glyph, and a 40px menu button with a visible focus ring. Hero (16px gutters): 11px mono eyebrow allowed to wrap to two lines; h1 at 40px / 1.0 holding two lines ('$10,000 a month,' / 'carried further.'); then the signal diagram folded flat into a stacked level bar directly under the headline: an ink rule, the blue origin dot beside 'Kristen, your account lead · Input · $10,000/mo Google Ad Grant', then three hairline-divided rows (COPD Foundation, UNCF, Solar Sister) each with name and '12 mo · FY · File' on the first line and a segmented vermilion bar (30/39/48% width, 8/10/12px tall, rising opacity) with the 24px value on the second; a dashed vertical tick at 14% crosses every bar and is labelled 'Google's 5% CTR floor'. The figcaption states that bar length shows order of reach, not scale. Then a three-line sub, a full-width 52px primary CTA with the 15 MIN tag, a full-width 48px ink-outline 'Am I eligible? · 2 MIN' button, and one line of fine print; the CTA sits at 594px and the eligibility button at 656px, both above a 760px fold, and the eligibility link is a button, not a text link. One trust element follows: the Letter from Google stamp, the Michelle Hurtado quote at 19px serif and her title with '780+ nonprofits served'. Below the fold the trust ledger becomes stacked rows (ticker as three cells, client roll as a two-line typographic wrap), the rules table becomes a definition list, the outcomes ledger becomes cards with the same six fields, the services meter keeps its seven bars at 60% height, and the team grid goes to two columns. Tap targets are 44px minimum; the ruled grid is dropped entirely on phones.
a11y: Target WCAG 2.2 AA across the system. Contrast, measured on the actual backgrounds: #12131A ink on paper 16.3:1; #3A3C48 body on paper 9.6:1; #5F6170 muted labels on paper 5.4:1 and on white 6.1:1; #4A4C58 client roll on paper 7.5:1; #B7311C small vermilion text (floor label, guarantee link) on paper 5.3:1; white on #C93A22 buttons 5.1:1 and on #B7311C 6.1:1; #E4432A signal on paper 3.6:1 so it is used only for the 60px/40px headline word and geometry, never for text under 24px; #B9BAC4 and #FF9A86 on the ink lead chip 9.6:1 and 9.0:1; #0A23A2 stamp on paper 10.4:1. Measured frame: desktop 829px (nav 76 + hero 600 + trust 153), phone CTA top at 594px and eligibility button at 656px inside a 760px fold; nothing overflows 1200px or 390px. Type floor: 11px for mono labels, 12px for chip units, 13px for chip names, 15-18px for everything else; no text is set below 11px anywhere. Diagram semantics: the arc field and the level bar are figures with aria-labelledby pointing to a visually hidden figcaption that states the argument (input, floor, three dated outcomes, and that geometry shows direction, not scale); the SVG geometry, rays, bars, origin ring, pins and menu glyph are aria-hidden decorative; every name, figure, period and case-file link is real DOM text in reading order (input first, then outcomes by distance); portrait placeholders carry role='img' with a descriptive label until real photographs replace them. Focus: a 2px #0A23A2 outline with 3px offset on every link and button via :focus-visible, visible on paper, white and ink backgrounds. Motion: every animation is inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, so reduced-motion users get the final static state with zero keyframes; nothing autoplays beyond the 1.4s load sequence and nothing loops. Pointer targets 44px on touch; buttons 52px. Headings are sentence case and uppercase is reserved for tracked mono labels. Print stylesheet keeps the ledger and the guarantee legible in black on white.

heroCopy.eyebrow: One of nine inaugural Google-certified Ad Grant agencies
heroCopy.headline: $10,000 a month, carried further.
heroCopy.sub: Google gives eligible nonprofits $10,000 a month in search ads. We acquire it, keep it above Google's 5% click-through floor, and tune it weekly so the people already searching for your cause find you first.

signatureMoments: The evidenced signal field: brand blue at the origin with the named account lead beside it, Google's 5% CTR floor as a dashed labelled innermost ring, and three real client outcomes pinned exactly where a ray meets an arc, each with vertical, twelve-month period and a case-file link, so the first screen is a sourced input/output record rather than a claim.

The level bar as the diagram's phone form: the same input, floor and three outcomes stacked as segmented vermilion bars under the headline, with a dashed floor tick crossing every bar, so the idea survives at 390px instead of shrinking.

The level-meter CTA: every 'Book a free call' button carries a 15 MIN mono tag and four rising bars that animate like a VU meter on hover, in pure CSS, a two-second brand memory that survives any Webflow edit.

The person-not-a-policy guarantee: Amber Snow's portrait, the line 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy' and the $25 promise sit directly under the primary CTA, turning the buried clause into the most quotable sentence on the site.

The trust ledger: a framed Letter from Google in 21px serif with the sender named, a dated status ticker (780+ / $48M+ / 100% · as of Sep 2026), and a typographic client roll in five voices between hairlines, replacing grey logo rows and thin stat lines.
dependencies: Name the account leads publicly and confirm the hero's lead name and portrait ('Kristen' in the mockups is a placeholder to be replaced by a real, consenting lead and a small colour photograph).

Verify and consent the three outcome chips with the clients: the figures, the twelve-month periods, the fiscal-year labels and the case-file numbers (COPD Foundation, UNCF, Solar Sister) must match the published case studies before launch.

Decide whether to publish a flat monthly fee range; if not, section 06 becomes 'flat monthly fee, no percentage of spend' with a quote CTA, and the direction keeps its structure but loses its strongest screening differentiator.
Approve the guarantee copy and page: Amber Snow's portrait, the 'person, not a policy' line and the $25 mechanism, with a real 'Read the guarantee' destination.

Fund a photography half-day: black-and-white eye-level portraits of the team plus small colour crops of Amber Snow and the named leads; the mockups ship with labelled CSS placeholder frames until then.
Consent from one client for a real redacted monthly report to appear in section 09 and as the 'See a real account report' PDF.
Redraw the megaphone mark as true vector and confirm its blue is #0A23A2 (the current site's hero is #0000FF); check Google Partner badge clear-space rules for the contained 'One of nine' band.
Webflow build with a locked class set (two heading classes, one figure class, the arc and level-bar components as embed symbols) and a style-guide page so editors cannot tip the signal into a siren.
Optional motion sprint: the hero and phone motion ship in CSS; GSAP + ScrollTrigger for sections 04-06 is a separately budgeted sprint with a reduced-motion audit.
risks: Red carries a second meaning: alarm, protest, error. The system depends on discipline (one vermilion word per headline, arcs never filled, max 3px strokes, errors in ink, small vermilion text only in #B7311C); lock the SVG tokens and the Webflow classes so a later editor cannot drift it.

Abstract geometry can still read as fintech or audio hardware if the human counterweights are cut. The named lead at the origin, Amber Snow under the CTA, the signed monthly note and black-and-white team photography are mandatory, not decorative.

Warm paper plus vermilion is a harder internal sell than blue. The mark tile, the blue origin dot, the Google stamp and the contained 'One of nine' band keep #0A23A2 visibly present, but 780 existing clients will notice the change and the wordmark lockup needs redrawing.

The bars and arcs encode order, not scale; the figcaptions say so, but a skeptical reader could still read '+3,000%' as a promise. Every figure ships with unit, period and a case-file link, and the sub-copy stays on reach and compliance rather than fundraising ROI.

Four Google font families (Bricolage Grotesque variable, Hanken Grotesk, Geist Mono, Instrument Serif) on Webflow need a font-loading budget and subsetting; drop Instrument Serif before dropping anything else.

The chips, ledger, checker and price range require NPM to commit to public numbers, periods and policy language; a 'no' on pricing or on named leads degrades the direction and should be answered before build.
